A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEMO3 research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched reliably, including the new Appendix A.3 in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic-simulation experiments across 16 tasks, including success rates, learning curves, component ablations and demonstration-efficiency analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports behavioral-cloning comparisons and examples of learned rewards during task execution.

M1.justification: The TD-MPC2 backbone, stage discriminators, reward construction, behavioral-cloning pretraining and transition to planning are unchanged. Algorithm 1, the training objectives and Appendix E architecture retain the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 16 tasks across ManiSkill manipulation, Meta-World, ManiSkill humanoids and Robosuite. The new reward visualizations use existing manipulation tasks; no additional domain or test environment is evaluated.

E2.justification: Figures 1 and 5 add behavioral cloning (BC) as a standalone comparator alongside the retained TD-MPC2, MoDem and LaNE baselines. BC already served as pretraining in v1, but was absent from these reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 6 revises the reported ManiSkill criteria: Stack Cube loses the explicit release requirement, Pick Place loses the static-at-goal qualifier, and Lift Peg Upright's second stage changes from close to upright to upright. These are documentation-level protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish that implementations changed or experiments were rerun. Budgets and other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 and Figure 15 examine learned rewards during successful, failed and partially successful rollouts, providing a qualitative check of whether rewards track task progress. Existing component ablations, demonstration-count sweeps and reward-granularity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averages and 95% confidence intervals for learning curves. The added BC comparison uses the existing reporting convention; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test or increased run count is documented.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds BC success rates of 7.6%, 18.0%, 24.0% and 31.0% for ManiSkill manipulation, Meta-World, ManiSkill humanoids and Robosuite, respectively. Figure 5 adds BC reference curves, and Figure 15 adds reward traces. Existing methods' numerical summaries and retained learning-curve findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, stage-label definition, reward transformation and loss equations are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical guarantees or proofs; the revised task-specific criteria in Table 6 concern experimental settings.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same method, task coverage and headline performance claims. Section 6 modestly qualifies the convergence claim, changing '4x faster' on the hardest tasks to 'up to 4x faster.'

C2.justification: Section 6 newly identifies simulation-only evaluation as a limitation and discusses untested transfer to physical robots under domain shift. It expresses optimism based on a prior pipeline's hardware transfer, while retaining the existing discussion of demonstration sources and sampling strategies.

D1.justification: v2 removes Section 4's direct repository link and code/environment availability statement, while retaining the abstract's project-site link. Contribution 3 changes a commitment to open-sourcing into 'are open-sourcing.' Architecture, numerical hyperparameters, demonstration-generation instructions and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; actual external availability cannot be determined from these wording changes.

R1.justification: The reference list, related-work section and Table 3 comparison remain unchanged. Section 6 adds a limited positioning argument by invoking Hansen et al. (2023)'s transfer to physical systems as precedent for DEMO3's proposed real-robot deployment.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and grammar edits, rewrites the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements, an impact statement and Appendix A.3. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 5 gain BC entries and legends, and a new Figure 15 presents rollout images with reward traces. Existing task and randomization illustrations are retained under new figure numbers. Smaller plot/table sizing changes and text reflow preserve the overall layout.

improvement.justification: The BC comparison provides useful context against imitation alone, the new reward traces make the learned signal easier to assess, and Section 6 more clearly acknowledges the absence of physical-robot validation. These modest gains improve the unchanged core study. Benefits are limited by less precise success-condition wording in Table 6 and the lack of separately documented setup details for the new BC comparator.
